# Review CHANGES REQUESTED for PAN-5482

# Review — PAN-5482
## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — guides/operating.mdx omits the emergency-stop CLI verb (FR-2) and implies `pan restore` brings back agents, which PAN-5549 says it does not

## Context
- Run ID: agent-pan-5482-review-07647eb9
- Manifest: /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-5482/.pan/review/agent-pan-5482-review-07647eb9/context.json
- Branch / workspace: feature/pan-5482 / /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-5482
- PR: https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/pull/5558
- HEAD reviewed: 07647eb932d90869542c3e4a6c4d0fa74680a026
- Base: merge-base 5cbd3edcbd5d (origin/main); prior cycle: none

The change is docs only (22 docs files plus `.pan/` plan artifacts). Most of it is accurate and well sourced: I re-traced
every high-value claim on the CI, Settings, Docs RAG, swarm and progressive-polyrepo pages to source and found them
correct. The two blockers are small, explicit requirement misses on the operating guide; each is a one or two
sentence fix.

## Blocking Findings

### [requirements] Operating guide does not name the emergency-stop CLI verb — `guides/operating.mdx:13`
- Severity: !
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect; in_pr_scope (FR-2, item `operating-guide`)
- Trigger and changed-code connection: FR-2 reads "It documents emergency stop: the CLI verb, the hotkey and the three
  dashboard entry points". The PRD background (G15) names the verb `pan admin cloister emergency-stop`. The new
  `## Stop every agent now` section lists the hotkey and the three dashboard entry points only. Note the spec
  conflict: W1 says "emergency stop, its four entry points", and the page implements exactly four (hotkey plus three
  dashboard entry points). FR-2 lists five and is the requirement the `operating-guide` item traces, so FR-2 governs;
  W1's "four" counts the dashboard-side entry points and does not exempt the CLI verb, which G15 documents first.
- Expected / observed / impact: expected the CLI verb; `grep -n 'emergency-stop\|cloister' guides/operating.mdx` matches
  only line 64 ("the emergency-stop freeze"). A terminal-only operator has no way to find the command from this page.
- Evidence: `pan admin cloister --help` prints `emergency-stop    Emergency stop - kill ALL agents immediately`
  (registered in `src/cli/commands/cloister/index.ts`, `.command('emergency-stop')`).
- Fix: add the verb to the section, for example a fifth bullet: "From a terminal, run `pan admin cloister emergency-stop`.
  It prints the agents it stopped and warns about any it could not confirm stopped." Paraphrase the help text; it
  contains a hyphen-dash only, no em dash. Update the intro count ("four ways") to match.

### [correctness] Backups section implies `pan restore` restores agents, contrary to the PAN-5549 re-check rule — `guides/operating.mdx:72`
- Severity: !
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect; in_pr_scope (FR-7; xBRIEF `operating-guide` Action:
  "Describe pan restore per the PAN-5549 re-check rule"; PRD rule 6 "Filed bugs (do not document as working)")
- Trigger and changed-code connection: the section says backups cover `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.claude/commands` and
  `~/.claude/agents`, then presents `pan restore` as "pick a backup to restore from" and "replacing the target folder"
  with no scope limit. PAN-5549 is not fixed: `src/cli/commands/restore.ts` maps only `claude-skills`/`skills` and
  `claude-commands`/`commands` targets (lines 65 to 68); there is no agents target.
- Expected / observed / impact: the PRD says "Today it restores skills and commands only, not agents" and requires the
  page to state today's behavior. An operator who restores after losing `~/.claude/agents` will expect agents back and
  will not get them.
- Evidence: static trace of `restore.ts` at HEAD; PRD `.pan/drafts/PAN-5482.md` line 204 and rule 6 (lines 74 to 81).
- Fix: say plainly that `pan restore` restores the skills and commands folders from a backup; the agents folder is
  backed up but not restored by `pan restore` today. Use no "known bug" wording (rule 6).

## Non-blocking Findings

Fix the first three in the same cycle; each is a one-line change.

- `~` [requirements] `integrations/ci.mdx:57`: the Get help section links Discord and Troubleshooting, not GitHub
  Issues. NFR-6 (traced by `ci-page`) reads "Each new page ends with the Get help section linking Discord and GitHub
  Issues", and the four other new pages use the shared sentence with both links. Use the same sentence as
  `guides/operating.mdx`. Kept non-blocking because the impact is negligible and no xBRIEF AC checks it.
- `~` [spec mismatch] PR #5558's body lacks `## Mintlify checks` and `## Found, not fixed`. PRD W17 asks for both in the
  PR body, but the xBRIEF `validate-and-record` ACs (ac1 to ac4) only require the checks to pass, and the work agent
  recorded the results in commit `2f4559e31e6`'s message. This is a PRD/xBRIEF inconsistency, not an implementation
  defect. The body looks generated by `pan done` (title "PAN-5482", checklist only), so a hand edit may be overwritten
  on the next `pan done`; add the two sections after the final `pan done`, or have the merger read the commit message.
- `~` [spec mismatch] `integrations/ci.mdx` does not contain the literal string `verification:` (PRD W3 AC lists it; the
  xBRIEF `ci-page.ac1` dropped it). The page uses `verification.tests` and `verification.tests: ci`, so the meaning is
  there. A two-line YAML example (`verification:` / `  tests: ci`) under `## Run tests on CI` would satisfy the PRD
  literally and help readers.
- `≉` `configuration/progressive-polyrepo.mdx:6` keeps a body H1 (`# Progressive polyrepo workspaces`) under the
  frontmatter `title`. The page is now published, so Mintlify will likely show a doubled heading. Several existing
  pages do the same (`configuration/auto-merge.mdx`, the `guides/` pages), and the recorded `mint validate` run reports
  51 pre-existing duplicate-h1 warnings; whether this file is among them was not verified. Dropping the line is a safe
  cleanup.
- `~` `cli/memory-commands.mdx` `## pan docs` table still lists `--scope session|project|global` (default `session`) for
  `disable`/`enable`. Those scopes are broken (PAN-5552) and NonGoal 4 says not to document them. The table is
  pre-existing and W15 only asked to fix the examples, so this is pre_existing; consider trimming the table to
  `--scope global` when PAN-5552 lands or in PAN-5503.
- `?` `features/swarm.mdx:7` says which mechanism an issue gets "depends on how it was started". The PRD decision says
  not to say which one a given issue gets, and no source was cited for this claim. Consider removing the clause.
- `≉` `configuration/progressive-polyrepo.mdx:84` says block-list groups and hyphenated names are "not read correctly
  today", and line 132 keeps the pre-existing phrase "evidence-blind workflow". Rule 6 asks for today's behavior with
  no known-bug framing; "Write each group on one line" already gives the instruction. "evidence-blind" is internal
  jargon.
- `~` `configuration/docs-rag.mdx` "What it indexes" omits `.claude/rules/*.md`, which `src/lib/docs/corpus.ts:81` also
  indexes (and the PRD lists).
- `?` `integrations/ci.mdx` lists test check names but omits the underscore form (`test_...`), which the matcher
  `/^tests?(?:\s*\(.*\)|[-_:].*|\s+\/\s+.*)?$/i` also accepts. Completeness only.
